portraits.printed_caption: Title Page Photo: This photograph of the Rohner family was taken in front of their first Benton County residence, the old Writsman home near Coffin Butte. Pictured with their parents are young Jake (b. 1914), Nellie (b. 1915), and Sam (b. 1916). All of the children were born in this house.

The caption is printed on the Acknowledgements page (front-3), not beneath the photo itself.

missing.title: Edward Sekermestrovich
missing.reason: No individual photograph of Edward Sekermestrovich appears anywhere in the monograph. Checked: cover (front-1, an early OSC School of Forestry work-crew group photo from Royal Jackson's collection -- not the narrator), title page (front-2), Acknowledgements (front-3), the CCC Company 3503 group photo (front-4), Table of Contents, "The Soap Creek Valley History Project" essay (p. i), "Introduction to Edward Sekermestrovich Interview" (p. ii), the opening page of the interview transcript, and the back-of-book "Background: Edward Sekermestrovich" biographical appendix (printed pp. 35-37, written by his wife Ida May Warner Sekermestrovich -- text only, no image) and the Index (p. 38). missing.title: Eugene Glender
missing.reason: The book's title-page photo (front-2) is captioned "Sisters Leone (left) and Elvera (right) Glender pose in front of the Glender family farmhouse in the early 1920s" -- it depicts narrator Eugene ("Gene") Glender's sisters, not Gene himself, and at any usable resolution the two figures are tiny, distant silhouettes in front of a farmhouse landscape rather than a portrait. No other photograph of Gene Glender appears in the front matter (checked cover, title page, Acknowledgements, Table of Contents, "The Soap Creek Valley History Project" essay, Soap Creek Valley map, and the Glender Tampico Tour map through printed page vi). Per instructions not to substitute a different photograph for a missing frontispiece/title-page portrait, none was selected. For the record: solo and family snapshots of Gene Glender DO exist much later in the book, in "Appendix B: Hunting Elephants in the Oregon Country" and "Appendix C: Family Photos" (around printed pp. 106-117) -- including a 1989 photo of the adult Gene Glender at the elephant-fossil spring site, photographed by Bob Zybach -- but these are deep interior/appendix material, not front matter, and were not used.
